lineage: fidelity probe p08_charts, 2026-09-24 (promoted by WP-G G-2, 2026-09-25)
notes: Findings F3d and F3g (docs/engine/fidelity/01-FINDINGS.md): chart specs a model plausibly writes - a type
alias (column_clustered), a type name nobody knows (grouped_bar), one series per bar with overlap 100 to colour
bars individually, values written as strings, a radar (not a chart object on Path A: PptxRender draws
nothing for it) and 24 labelled bars. This is the one family that keeps specs the contract rejects, on
purpose: they are what the charts package (C) made fail visibly, in the validator, the linter, the preview
and the export alike. The HTML is the probe's but for one line: the heading has width:872px, to layout-06's
title zone's right edge (see flexgrid's notes; the probe's title overhung by 6 px through the test masters'
manifest/theme mismatch).
Placeholder: the heading is the slide's title placeholder by its data-placeholder=title, although it sits at top 16
and only 55 % of its box lies inside layout-06's title zone (from y 28.8) - since render-check R3 (2026-09-29)
page.js records the attribute and map_placeholders' pass 1 honours it. Before, geometry alone decided and caption
A, wholly inside the zone, took the title; now the zone is claimed and caption A is a text box. Each keeps its

measured rect, so the gate is unchanged (953 px2 before and after). The mapping is asserted, not only documented: test_torture.test_the_listed_placeholders_are_the_mapped_ones holds every elements[] entry that names a placeholder (or null), and its startsWith (the heading's, not caption A's).
text 7 = the heading 1 + the six captions A-F. chart 6: every data-chart div is an authored chart element in the
extracted IR - the extractor does not judge specs - and the recogniser finds nothing to add (recognised 0).
The chain for the two rejected specs, measured on 2026-09-25: charts_spec.validate rejects B ('unknown chart
type 'grouped_bar' (did you mean 'bar'?)') and E ('chart type 'radar' is not a chart object on Path A');
lint reports each as a chart-spec error (expectedLint 2); IR.validate() raises the same two messages on the
chart elements, which judge_family counts as those lint findings rather than new problems (G-2's
torture_expect.py, reached from judge_family by one call-site line); the extractor neither rasters nor drops them and writes no diagnostic; the
emitter rolls each back to a labelled placeholder shape named '<name> (chart not built)', with an emit warning
and failed/error on its emit-report entry - never a half-built chart (Peter #8). The deck holds 4 chart parts.
The lenient specs build, with advisories (Peter #8): A resolves to column (chart-advisory warn 'read as
'column''); D's four numeric strings are read as numbers (4 chart-advisory warns, one per value, and one emit
note each); C and F build silently. expectedLint: chart-spec 2 errors, chart-advisory 5 warns.
Chart frames are masked in the pixel gate (decision #7), so the gate number here is the captions and the
title; the placeholders' boxes are the chart boxes and are masked too. The text row cannot pair the two
placeholder shapes with an IR text element and counts them as unmatched (2), which is not a finding.

gateMaxPx2 1,144 = 953 px2 masked, measured 2026-09-25 on main 4ab1be8 (fidelity-w2 + X, plan 16 #22) + G-2, references rendered in Calibri / Calibri Light; two runs, identical, + 20 % (Peter #16, plan 11). Of it:

all 953 px2 are the heading - test-16x9's manifest/theme mismatch (G-1 open item 14, D item 17): the browser draws the 700 heading in Calibri Light with synthetic bold, advances unchanged (Edge, measured in weights' notes), while PptxRender, like PowerPoint, draws the file's +mj-lt b=1 through the theme part's major font as Calibri Bold, ~3 % wider and heavier. Chart frames and the two placeholders are masked.

gateMaxPx2 1,144 = max(measured x 1.2, measured + 60) over the measured 953 px2 masked non-chart area on fidelity-w3 (2314d7f), 2026-09-25 (plan §11; Peter #16: measured + 20 %, with the 60 px2 per-slide noise tolerance as the floor). A regression guard, not a target.
